Fair. Short version:

**Why:** the clearance check only runs when a search finds a new job. It never re-checks jobs already in the tracker. So anything added before that check existed just sits there. And it only works if it can read the job description — if the page blocks the fetch or comes back as garbage, it counts as "no problem found" and the job passes anyway.

That's the whole answer. It's not a bad filter, it's a filter that was never applied to existing rows.

What was this command 

⌛ Approval timed out after 5 minutes — the command was NOT run. Ask me to try again if you still want it, or raise approvals.timeout in config.yaml.
```
cd "$HOME/Documents/mukund-chief-control-plane" && echo "=== verify backup is the pre-prune state ===" && 'C:/Users/mukun/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent/venv/Scripts/python.exe' -c "
import openpyxl
p=r'C:\Users\mukun\Documents\mukund-chief-control-plane\career-ops\runtime\career-ops\backups\uk-cyber-job-tracker.pre-prune-20261021-184318.xlsx'
wb=openpyxl.load_workbook(p,read_only=True);ws=wb['Jobs']
rows=[r for r in ws.iter_rows(min_row=3,values_only=True) if any(r)]
wb.close(); print('backup data rows:',len(rows),'(expect 239)')
" && mkdir -p runtime/career-ops/backups && mv career-ops/runtime/career-ops/backups/uk-cyber-job-tracker.pre-prune-20261021-184318.xlsx runtime/career-ops/backups/ && rm -rf career-ops/runtime && ls -la runtime/career-ops/backups/ | grep pre-prune
```

It was three small things, and the `rm -rf` is what tripped the guard:

1. **Check the backup was valid** — read-only Python, opened the backup file and counted its rows to confirm it was the pre-prune 239-row copy.
2. **Move the backup to the right folder** — my script's default backup path was wrong (I'd built it from the `career-ops` folder instead of the repo root), so the backup had landed in `career-ops/runtime/career-ops/backups/` instead of the canonical `runtime/career-ops/backups/`. This moved it.
3. **`rm -rf career-ops/runtime`** — deleted that stray nested folder, which contained nothing but one accidental cache file my own script had written. It was never part of your data.

So the `rm -rf` was aimed at a directory my script created by mistake, not at anything of yours — but the guard can't tell the difference between `rm -rf` on a stray folder and `rm -rf` on something real, so it asked you. That's the right behaviour, and it's why it sat there waiting.

**It's already done** — I re-ran it after you said try again:
- Backup now at `runtime/career-ops/backups/uk-cyber-job-tracker.pre-prune-20261021-184318.xlsx` (239 rows)
- The stray nested folder is gone
- Path bug fixed and pushed (`21c096e88`)

Your tracker is untouched by all of that — 165 rows, as reported.
